reading: The input is the left half of a closed symmetric outline. Mirror it about a vertical axis just right of its rightmost column to close it. The output is only the filled interior of the closed outline, in the outline colour; the outline itself is erased.
verb: complete by mirror, keep filled interior

slots.half: the single fg object (left half of an outline)
slots.axis: vertical line just right of the object's max column (x' = 2*maxX+1-x)
slots.interior: bg cells enclosed by half plus its mirror image
slots.rest: everything else, including the outline, becomes bg

why: on every pair the output's non-bg cells are exactly the cells strictly inside the mirrored-closed outline

reading: A 5 pivot has an arm of 2s. The arm is rotated 90 degrees clockwise about the pivot (same length, still colour 2), and the cells of the old arm become 3.

slots.arm: the straight run of 2s touching the pivot

why: on every pair the new 2-run starts next to the 5, has the old arm's length, and points in the old direction turned clockwise; old arm cells are 3

reading: Each square outline of 5 has its hollow interior filled with a colour chosen by the interior size: 1x1 -> 6, 2x2 -> 7, 3x3 -> 8.

slots.subject: each enclosed bg hole inside a 5 square outline
slots.colour: lookup by hole side length: 1->6, 2->7, 3->8 (learned from train)

why: every enclosed hole is filled entirely with the colour its size maps to; nothing outside the holes changes

reading: The 1xN row with a single 2 at the centre column c becomes an NxN grid: the 2 sends two diagonal lines down-left and down-right to the edges (a V), and every cell strictly below/inside the V with (x - y) mod 4 == c mod 4 becomes 1.

slots.size: N x N where N is the input width
slots.hatch: colour 1 on diagonals x - y == c (mod 4), only on bg cells inside/below the V

why: on every pair the 2 cells form the V from the apex and the 1 cells are exactly the inside-V cells on the period-4 down-right diagonals aligned with the apex column

reading: Every full row or full column made of one colour (always the 0 colour here) is recoloured to 2; all other cells stay.

new_rows.name: full_line
new_rows.datalog:
w(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
h(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
rowc(Y, C, count(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
colc(X, C, count(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
frow(Y) :- rowc(Y, C, N), w(M), N = M + 1.
fcol(X) :- colc(X, C, N), h(M), N = M + 1.
full_line(Y, X) :- frow(Y), px(Y, X, C).
full_line(Y, X) :- fcol(X), px(Y, X, C).

why: every cell of a single-colour full row or column (colour 0) becomes 2 (key 0->2); no other cell changes
invariants: all cells not on a full uniform line

reading: The 3x3 input is scaled to a 3x3 arrangement of blocks: a block holds a copy of the input exactly where the input cell has the input's most common colour; other blocks are empty.
why: every output block is the input or all 0, and the copies sit at the positions of the input's most common (background) colour
invariants: the unit is the whole input unchanged

reading: Full columns of the background colour cut the grid into column bands, each with one other colour. In each band the background cells take the colour of the next band to the right (the last band takes the first band's colour).

slots.panels: column bands cut by full columns of the background colour
slots.subject: background cells inside each band
slots.colour: the single non-bg colour of the next band, cyclically (last -> first)

why: on every pair each band's bg cells become the next band's colour; separator columns and non-bg cells are unchanged

reading: Each 4x4 hollow square has 4-cell lines of 1 on some grid edges aligned with it. The square is repeated with period 4 from its position toward each such edge until the grid border (clipped there); the 1 markers are overwritten.

slots.directions: each grid edge carrying a 1-line aligned with the square's rows or columns

why: on every pair the output is the squares plus their period-4 repeats along each marked direction, and no 1 remains

reading: Some solid rectangles carry a one-cell-wide tail line. Each such rectangle slides along its tail's direction by the tail length and the tail is erased; moved rectangles are drawn on top, and parts of other rectangles that were hidden under them are restored to full rectangles.

slots.subject: each rectangle with a protruding 1-wide tail of its colour
slots.layering: moved rectangles over static ones; static rectangles completed to their full box

why: on every pair each tailed rectangle keeps its shape and is shifted by its tail length in the tail direction, with no tail left
invariants: rectangles without tails (completed to full box)

reading: The input is tiled 3x3. Then every non-zero cell's whole row is filled with 1 (keeping the coloured cells), and the cell diagonally up-left and the cell diagonally down-right of each coloured cell become 3 (clipped at the border).

slots.row_fill: colour 1 on bg cells of every row containing a coloured cell
slots.diag: colour 3 at (y-1,x-1) and (y+1,x+1) of every coloured cell in the tiled grid

why: on every pair the output equals the 3x3 tiling with 1-rows through coloured cells and 3s on their up-left and down-right diagonals
invariants: the coloured cells of each tile copy
